institutions.title: Rebelión de An Lushan y sus sucesores
institutions.text: La rebelión iniciada en755 afecta a los centros Tang y a la organización militar regional. El punto de Chang’an es una referencia del conflicto; no dibuja un frente continuo ni convierte toda la dinastía en territorio rebelde.
institutions.note: Contexto parcial; cronología de fuente y localización no equivalen a control diario.

institutions.title: Restauración Tang y accesos al trono
institutions.text: Zhongzong, el breve reinado deShang en710, Ruizong y Xuanzong tienen accesos distintos. Xuanzong del sigloVIII no es Xuānzong del IX; las regencias y dignidades de retiro tampoco equivalen al mismo cargo.
institutions.note: Contexto parcial; cronología de fuente y localización no equivalen a control diario.

governance.note: Forma de organización; no una evaluación contemporánea ni control territorial homogéneo.

record.label: Imperio Tang · restauración y poderes regionales
record.note: Zhou de Wu Zetian700–704 se resuelve como entidad propia; restauración Tang705, rebelión de An Lushan755–763. No se afirma control uniforme de toda la superficie.

geography.note: Componentes originales completos, con propiedades e índices conservados; sin simplificación añadida.

reignFields.raw: 18 May 762<ref name=BT11/><ref>According to Daizong's biography in the ''[[Old Book of Tang]]'', he assumed the throne on the ''jisi'' day in the 4th month of the 1st year of the Baoying era of Tang Suzong's/Daizong's reign. This date corresponds to 18 May 762 in the Julian calendar.(「(宝应元年四月)己巳，即皇帝位于柩前。」) ''Old Book of Tang'', vol. 11.</ref> – 10 June 779

June 12, 779<ref name="Reign Start">According to Li Kuo's biography in the ''[[Old Book of Tang]]'', he assumed the throne on the ''guihai'' day in the 5th month of the 14th year of the ''Dali'' era of Tang Daizong's reign. This date corresponds to 12 June 779 in the Julian calendar.(「大历十四年五月...。癸亥，即位于太极殿」) ''Old Book of Tang'', vol. 12.</ref> – February 25, 805

27 February 684<ref name=start1st>Volume 203 of the ''[[Zizhi Tongjian]]'' recorded that Ruizong was made emperor under Wu Zetian on the ''jiwei'' day of the 2nd month of the 1st year of the Guangzhai era of his reign. This date corresponds to 27 Feb 684 in the Gregorian calendar. {{bracket|{{lang|zh|(光宅元年二月)己未，立雍州牧豫王旦為皇帝。}}}} ''Zizhi Tongjian'', vol. 203.</ref><ref name=ZZTJ203>''[[Zizhi Tongjian]]'', [[:zh:s:資治通鑑/卷203|vol. 203]].</ref> – 16 October 690<ref name=end1st>Volume 204 of the ''[[Zizhi Tongjian]]'' recorded that the dynastic change from Tang to Wu Zhou took place on the ''renwu'' day of the 9th month of the first year of the Tianshou era of Wu Zetian's reign. This date corresponds to 16 Oct 690 in the Gregorian calendar. {{bracket|{{lang|zh|(天授元年九月)壬午，御则天数，...，以唐为周，改元。}}}} ''Zizhi Tongjian'', vol. 204.</ref><ref name=ZZTJ204>''Zizhi Tongjian'', [[:zh:s:資治通鑑/卷204|vol. 204]].</ref>
25 July 710<ref name=ZZTJ209>''Zizhi Tongjian'', [[:zh:s:資治通鑑/卷209|vol. 209]].</ref> – 8 September 712<ref name=ZZTJ210>''Zizhi Tongjian'', [[:zh:s:資治通鑑/卷210|vol. 210]].</ref>
8 July<ref name=ZZTJ209>''Zizhi Tongjian'', [[:zh:s:資治通鑑/卷209|vol. 209]].</ref> – 25 July 710<ref name=ZZTJ209/>

12 August 756<ref name=Ascension>Following the rebellion of [[An Lushan]], Emperor Suzong was proclaimed emperor by the army on August 12, 756, but his father [[Emperor Xuanzong of Tang|Emperor Xuanzong]] and his retinue, who had escaped to [[Sichuan]], only heard the news on September 10, 756, that date marking the end of Xuanzong's reign in practice. Until Emperor Xuanzong received the news of Emperor Suzong's ascension, he continued to issue imperial edicts as emperor.</ref><ref name=startreign>According to Suzong's biography in the ''[[Old Book of Tang]]'', he assumed the throne at Lingwu on the ''jiazi'' day in the 7th month of the 15th year of the ''Tianbao'' era of Tang Xuanzong's reign. This corresponds to 12 Aug 756 in the Julian calendar. ([天宝十五载七月]是月甲子，上即皇帝位于灵武。) ''Old Book of Tang'', vol. 10.</ref><ref name=BT10>''[[Old Book of Tang]]'', [[:zh:s:舊唐書/卷10|vol. 10]].</ref> – 16 May 762

8 September 712<ref>He ascended the throne following the abdication of his father [[Emperor Ruizong of Tang|Emperor Ruizong]] in 712, who received the title ''[[Taishang Huang]]'' (retired emperor) but continued to wield actual imperial power until 713.</ref><ref name=Ascension>Volume 210 of ''[[Zizhi Tongjian]]'' recorded that Tang Ruizong (by then the [[Taishang Huang]]) released an edict, declaring that Emperor Xuanzong was to be solely in charge of the empire's affairs. This edict was released on the ''yichou'' day of the 7th month of the 1st year of the Kaiyuan era of Tang Xuanzong's reign. This date corresponds to 30 Jul 713 in the Gregorian calendar. Three days later, on the ''wuchen'' day of the same month, which corresponds to 2 August 713 on the Gregorian calendar, Princess Taiping was forced to commit suicide. With the death of Princess Taiping, the last major obstacle to Xuanzong's control was removed. [(开元元年七月)乙丑，上皇诰：...太平公主逃入山寺，三日乃出，赐死于家,...]</ref> – 12 August 756<ref>Following the rebellion of [[An Lushan]], Xuanzong's son [[Emperor Suzong of Tang|Emperor Suzong]] was proclaimed emperor by the army on  12 August 756, but Emperor Xuanzong and his retinue, who had escaped to [[Sichuan]], only heard the news on  10 September 756, that date marking the end of Xuanzong's reign in practice. Until Emperor Xuanzong received the news of Emperor Suzong's ascension, he continued to issue imperial edicts as emperor.</ref><ref name=endreign>According to Tang Suzong's biography in the ''[[Old Book of Tang]]'', he assumed the throne at Lingwu on the ''jiazi'' day in the 7th month of the 15th year of the Tianbao era of Tang Xuanzong's reign. This date corresponds to 12 August 756 in the Gregorian calendar.(「(天宝十五载七月)是月甲子，上即皇帝位于灵武。」) ''Old Book of Tang'', vol. 10.</ref>

3 January 684<ref>Volume 203 of the ''[[Zizhi Tongjian]]'' recorded that Zhongzong was made emperor under Wu Zetian on the ''jia'zi'' day of the 12th month of the 1st year of the ''Hong'dao'' era of Tang Gaozong's reign. This date corresponds to 3 Jan 684 in the Julian calendar. {{bracket|{{lang|zh|(弘道元年)十二月，...甲子，中宗即位，...}}}} ''Zizhi Tongjian'', vol. 203.</ref> – 26 February 684<ref>Volume 203 of the ''[[Zizhi Tongjian]]'' recorded that Zhongzong was deposed by his mother [[Wu Zetian|Empress Wu]] on the ''wu'wu'' day of the 2nd month of the 1st year of the ''Guang'zhai'' era of Tang Ruizong's reign. This date corresponds to 23 Jan 684 in the Julian calendar. {{bracket|{{lang|zh|(光宅元年)二月，戊午，太后集百官于乾元殿，裴炎与中书侍郎刘祎之、羽林将军程务挺、张虔勖勒兵入宫，宣太后令，废中宗为庐陵王，扶下殿。}}}} ''Zizhi Tongjian'', vol. 203; Wu then made Zhongzong's brother Ruizong her next puppet emperor.</ref>

23 February 705<ref>Restored as emperor three days after the coup that put an end to his mother's power. Volume 207 of the ''[[Zizhi Tongjian]]'' recorded that Zhongzong assumed the throne on the ''bingwu'' day of the 1st month of the 1st year of the Shenlong era of Wu Zetian's reign. This date corresponds to 23 Feb 705 in the Gregorian calendar. {{bracket|{{lang|zh|(神龙元年正月)丙午，中宗即位。}}}} ''Zizhi Tongjian'', vol. 207. </ref> – 3 July 710
